title: Protocols and Structural Typing
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and behaviour of Protocols and Structural Typing.
Choose an appropriate protocols and structural typing technique for a Python application.
Interpret representative code and output involving protocols and structural typing.
Identify limitations and failure modes for protocols and structural typing.
Apply protocols and structural typing concepts in maintainable Python code.

understand.concept: A Protocol describes an interface by the operations an object provides rather than requiring inheritance from a particular base class. This is structural typing: an object is suitable when it has the required members with compatible types. Protocols support flexible APIs, adapters and test doubles. runtime_checkable enables limited member-presence checks, not full behavioural verification.
understand.whyItMatters: Protocols let components depend on capabilities instead of concrete implementations, reducing coupling.
understand.analogy: A power plug works with any compatible socket standard, regardless of manufacturer.
understand.analogyLimit: A compatible-looking object may still behave incorrectly; a protocol describes shape, not full behavioural guarantees.
understand.summary: Protocols and Structural Typing develops practical application engineering skills for Python projects.

explain.narrative:
## Program to capabilities
Define a protocol with the methods or attributes a consumer needs. A class can satisfy it without explicitly inheriting from it. Use protocols for service boundaries such as storage, clocks or notification senders. Keep protocols small and focused. Runtime protocol checks inspect member presence rather than fully verifying signatures or semantics, so use static checking and tests for stronger confidence.

questions.prompt: What is structural typing based on?
questions.answer: Whether an object provides the required members
options: Whether an object provides the required members
Whether it inherits from one exact base class
Whether its source file is named correctly
questions.explanation: Structural typing checks the available interface rather than explicit ancestry.

questions.prompt: Must a class explicitly inherit from a Protocol to satisfy it?
questions.explanation: A compatible class can satisfy a protocol implicitly.

questions.prompt: What does a protocol primarily describe?
questions.explanation: Protocols specify methods and attributes expected by consumers.

questions.prompt: Why use a fake implementation in tests?
questions.answer: To replace an external dependency predictably
options: To replace an external dependency predictably
questions.explanation: A fake can make tests deterministic and independent of external services.

questions.prompt: Does runtime_checkable prove method semantics are correct?
questions.explanation: Runtime protocol checks are limited and do not establish behavioural correctness.
